utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, everybody, and welcome. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. Mr. Brdjanin, can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. It's Joanna Korner, Julian Nicholls, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And good morning to you. Mr. Cunningham, appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm David Cunningham I'm here with Aleksandar Vujic for the defendant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Thank you and good morning to you too. Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic. We are proceeding with your testimony today. I just want to remind you that your testimony continues on the solemn declaration you made yesterday. You don't need to repeat it today, but I am reminding you that you are under the same oath. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that there are no preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: There are none from our side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sir, when we left off yesterday, we were talking about the physical plan, if you will, of the ARK Crisis Staff. I want you now to tell us how decisions were reached. You told us yesterday that at some point, the Crisis Staff became more a collection of municipal officials and assemblymen. What I'd like to do is have you focus in on the way decisions were reached prior to that time, that is, prior to the time it became more of a body of people from municipalities. So having said that, could you tell us how decisions were reached when this was a - and this is going to be my phrase - when it was primarily a group of individuals from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember all of the details. It was a long time ago, and I really can't remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'd like for you to tell us what you can remember. You said you can't remember all the details. That implies that you can remember some of the details. So tell the Chamber as best as you can how the decisions were reached.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember all of those details.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Can you remember anything about the way meetings were like when members of the municipalities became the main participants in the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were meetings. There were deputies there as well as representatives of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm afraid I can't remember any of the details as to how this looked like. I told you what I remember, and I told you yesterday. I can't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: But I want to remind you that you also told me something different in Banja Luka and something different in a proofing session. You have no recollection of what you told me in those sessions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I don't know if that's a proper question to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know how your system works.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know either, but I've never heard a question like that before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In my system, which we didn't borrow from Ms. Korner's, we borrowed it from the Scots, I wouldn't allow it. So I do realise the problem, but if you can rephrase it, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If -- can I put it this way, Your Honour, I have no objection if this witness made a statement in writing from which he wishes to refresh his memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I apologise for interrupting. If there would have been a statement, it would have been provided to you; he did not make a statement in writing. With your permission, I'll proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, but do try to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you remember when the ARK Crisis Staff consisted primarily or the majority of the people came from the municipalities -- do you remember what the main topics of conversation were at the ARK Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The topics were all contained in the conclusions. Whatever is in the conclusions that were passed by the Crisis Staff were the topics of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: If I could show the witness Exhibit 227, Prosecutor's Exhibit 227, which is the first set of published opinions of the ARK Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to go to entry number 3, which is on page 4 of the English translation. I direct your attention to entry number 5 under the conclusions. Have you read that conclusion before, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That conclusion deals with security measures at the Laktasi airport. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Laktasi airport or the Banja Luka airport by the Laktasi Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It deals with the Banja Luka airport which is actually in Laktasi.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: But having said that, it deals with the airport. Right, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you know if this provision was ever implemented?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the same exhibit, entry number 13. That is in -- on page -- appears to be page 23 of the English version. If we look at conclusion number 5, there is another provision that says: "The Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Laktasi is to implement immediately the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and place a barrier on the road to the Banja Luka airport along the Banja Luka/Bosanska Gradiska main road." Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Does it appear to you by 20 May, the date of this conclusion, that that provision had ever been implemented?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by this here, it was not implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to entry number 3, the first time that this provision is talked about. That is the conclusion reflected in the Gazette on English page 4. Looking at those conclusions, the remainder of those conclusions, do you have any idea which, if any of those conclusions, were ever implemented?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's go to the next page in the Gazette, entry Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. number 4, English page 5, the listing of the conclusions of the Crisis Staff of 8 May, 1992. I'm going to talk to you about three specific conclusions. Look at conclusion number 3. Read that conclusion to yourself and let me know when you're done reading.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That obviously has to do with paramilitaries. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you happen to have any recollection of the discussion at the Crisis Staff related to this as to whether the discussion was concerned with Serb paramilitaries, Croat paramilitaries, Muslim paramilitaries? Can you shed any light on the who the paramilitaries they're talking about are?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applied to all the paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Was there any distinction made between Serb and non-Serb paramilitaries, or was the desire to disarm all paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To disarm everybody but an emphasis was put on the Serb paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Read conclusion number 8 to yourself. This deals with refugees. And let me know when you're done reading.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the refugees to come back home, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Right. Have you read that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When that conclusion was issued, did it have any impact on those refugees? That is, after the conclusion appeared in the ARK Gazette, did the refugees go back to their homes?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The final one I want to ask you about specifically here is number 13, and this deals with Professor Mirjanic being appointed to replace Mr. Kuzmanovic. That's what we had talked about yesterday. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Take these conclusions as a whole. Read them to yourself. I know you've read these conclusions before, but if you need time to read them now do so because I want to ask you which, if any, of these conclusions were implemented, if you know.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me to read all the 13 conclusions? I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Yes, read all 13 to yourself, and then tell us based on that reading which, if any, of those conclusions were ever implemented.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because sometimes I'm baffled by some answers. Number 1, Professor Dragoljub Mirjanic is hereby appointed a new member of the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina replacing Ratko Kuzmanovic. Do you remember this happening? Because you yourself yesterday said that at a very early stage --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this was implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This was implemented, so you know it was implemented.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Beyond that, do you know if any of the other decisions were ever implemented, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, please, can you start from number 1 and we go down so that the public can see what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether any other conclusions were implemented, save for the one under number 13. I really don't remember whether any other conclusions were ever implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move ahead, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Entry number 6 in Prosecutor 227 on English page 13 are the conclusions of the Crisis Staff meeting, 9 May 1992. I want to first of all direct your attention to entry number 2. Specifically, the third paragraph under entry number 2 which reads as follows: "Decisions adopted by the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina are to be strictly respected in all public and economic organisations." Do you recall why it was necessary, why someone felt it was necessary to put such a statement in to these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Reading the remainder of the conclusions to yourself, I want to ask you the same question. Do you have any recollection of any of these other conclusions being implemented?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that only the decision under number 7 was applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. And what is your recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about parts of enterprises whose headquarters were in other republics of the former state. By this decision, they were unable to continue their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about the subject matter of number 6, which deals with various travel agencies in Banja Luka? Do you have any recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Travel agencies started charging a lot of money for the air tickets that they were selling to people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Look at number 5, because that deals with the question of the disarmament of paramilitary formations. Consistent with your prior testimony, the presence of that conclusions there, would it be indicative of the fact that that was a topic of discussion that day?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here: "We appeal to the presidents of the National Defence Council to take immediate steps to disarm paramilitary formations." So an appeal was made for the formations to be disarmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Cunningham. Have you finished with number 5, or do you still have questions on number 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm done with number 5, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let me ask to make sure that I'm understanding the witness well. So in other words, you mean to tell us, Mr. Blagojevic, that although this decision was taken, divided into three parts, the first one being an appeal for the disarming; the second, the establishing of a deadline by which the disarming had to -- or the weapons were to be turned over; and the third, establishing the sanction, firm action should be taken. Do you mean to tell us that this decision had absolutely no follow-up, no one took any steps to disarm the paramilitary formation? No one ever mentioned or established the 11th of May 1992 or any subsequent or other date by which weapons were to turn over? And that absolutely nothing, and nothing happened to those who refused to turn illegally owned weapon and ammunition? Is this your version? Is this your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see here that an appeal was made to take measures. I don't know whether anything was actually done in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told there might be a possible error in the translation of his answer at 8:25, so with the Court's permission, I would re-ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sir, a minute ago, we were talking about entry number 7 which had to deal with business enterprises. And I asked you the following question, it's reflected on page 8, line 23: "And what is your recollection of that?" Your answer was: "We're talking about parts of enterprises whose headquarters were in other republics of the former state. By this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. decision, they were unable to continue their work." My case manager says that he believes that there's an error in translation. So what would your answer be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can suggest to the witness, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did they get the translation correct? Is that what the effect of number 7 was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually I will put it myself. Did you say that by virtue of this decision that they were unable to continue their work or did you say by virtue of this decision they were able to continue their work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They could continue their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That explains it. That is what you meant, Mr. Cunningham, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fair, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness a new exhibit, but I want to keep 227 at the ready because he's going to be looking at it again. I want to show you P182, which is a decision 9 May 1992, by the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want you to read that exhibit 182 if you have the Serbian version in front of you. Once you get it, read it.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All the decisions and" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Go ahead and read it to yourself. You don't need to read it out loud. When you're done, I'll ask you a question about it. Ready? You were at the meeting, I take it. Why was it necessary to put such a statement in a decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Are the people -- are the municipalities or other entities complying with ARK Crisis Staff conclusions at this point?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were complying or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why this statement would be put in there?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were probably not complying in reality, and that must have been the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's being -- pushing it too far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would leave it for the cross-examination, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rather than raise it as an objection now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to go to a new exhibit. I'd like to look at P184. Then I'll come back to 227. And just to let the usher know, the next exhibit after that will be 187, so that we can move ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Noticing also the date of this document and the proximity with the establishment of the Autonomous Region -- the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Actually, Judge, I made a mistake. I mean to go to 227. I apologise to the Court and counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to go back to P227, entry number 7. Should be the conclusions of 11 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: This is reflected at page 15 of the Gazette. Entry number 4 reads as follows: "The work of the Crisis Staff of the ARK is given full support." Do you have any recollection why that provision was put in there?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably because there were some who did not recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And when you say "some that did not recognise it," what do you mean when you identify them as "some"? Who is it that doesn't recognise it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a considerable part of the municipality supported the principle of regionalisation. Similarly, quite a few municipalities were in favour of the centralisation principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. So having said that, how does that tie into your answer that some did not recognise it? Those municipalities that, as you put it, that were in favour of centralisation?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, even at those meetings, there was some controversy among those who attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Tell us what you -- identify what you mean by those meetings. Are you talking about ARK Crisis Staff meetings or other meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I meant the meetings of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Could you tell us more about what you mean when you say that there was some controversy among those who attended. How did this controversy express itself? Was this expressed during the ARK Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Some people openly advocated this principle of centralisation of organs or bodies, whereas others preferred regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And those bodies that advocated centralisation, what was their position with respect to the authority or competence of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sure. You told us that there were people at meetings who advocated regionalisation; others that advocated centralisation. Those that advocated centralisation, did they think that the ARK Crisis Staff was a competent organ or lacked competence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that in the translation, that in the interpretation the word "competent" and "competence" are being translated in the legal connotation in which they are being put by you, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not being asked to confirm whether these persons who opted for centralisation rather than regionalisation had their own idea on the capabilities of the ARK Crisis Staff. But basically, on whether the ARK Crisis Staff had jurisdiction, had the competence, in other words, the legal competence, to take decisions. This is what you're being asked. It has got nothing to do with competence in the sense of expertise and ability to do something, knowing how to do it. But we're talking of you're a lawyer by profession, so you should know what I am talking about. Legal competence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under the regulations that were in force then, the Crisis Staff did not have jurisdiction because it was not established under a government decision or any -- by a decision of any other republican body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this was your personal opinion, or the personal opinion and stand taken by others, by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my opinion. I don't know what the others thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What did the others complain about, then? Those who preferred centralisation rather than regionalisation? What was their objection? Did they just say "we don't like you, we don't recognise you because we shouldn't be dealing with this Crisis Staff on a regional basis but on a national centralised basis"? What was being said in the meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, people objected for the most part to the allocation of funds, the way funds were distributed, because funds were kept in the reserves of the region, and they were not allowed to go on to the budget of the republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have my sympathy, Mr. Cunningham. I'm at a loss, so I return him back to you. Maybe you'll be more successful than I have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let's go to a new exhibit. Let's look at P187 which ironically enough deals with finances. This is a decision of 11 May 1992 by the ARK Crisis Staff. I don't have it in Serbian. I'm sorry. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What are you looking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I've got it, Your Honour. I had a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you need it in Serbo-Croat, I can give it to you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sir, this is a decision dealing with the financing of the institution in defence of the ARK directing that all the municipalities within the Krajina deposit money on a per capita basis into a specific account. Read that to yourself, make sure that I've described it fairly. And when you're done reading it to yourself, I'd like to ask you a question. Do you remember this decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Is this one of the decisions of the financing that you were talking about just a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Was money ever deposited into the account reflected in there, or any money ever paid over to the ARK that you recalled from these municipalities?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these funds were never paid because the municipalities were at that time applying the laws enacted by the National Assembly including the law on turnover tax and tax and services under which they paid contributions and dues. But the point is that these funds did not go to the budget of the republic. They went, instead, to various funds in the territory of the autonomous region. This decision was never applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know of any municipality that was ever sanctioned for not paying funds as you've just described?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it possible, Mr. Blagojevic, that you were not being kept informed and that these funds or these deposits may have actually taken place, and you are simply not aware of them, or not aware of the fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're a hundred per cent sure that no municipality ever paid these 30 dinars per citizen to this transfer account number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly not in 1992. In 1992, I'm sure they were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Back to Exhibit P227, I'm going to go to entry number 9. English translation is on page 17.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which date is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It should be 13 May 1992, and specifically I want you to look at conclusion number 4 which reads as follows: "The Security Services Centre in Banja Luka is to fully implement the decisions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina on the disarming of illegal paramilitary units and individuals who are in possession of weapons and ammunition." Which paramilitaries was the Crisis Staff referring to?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably referring to all paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: We know from your prior review and your prior testimony that this is a topic that is brought up several times in the conclusions. Do you know why it was necessary - thank you - why it was necessary or felt necessary to put the language that the Security Services Centre is to fully implement the decisions? Do you know why that is?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this decision was enforced. That is the only reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let me take you to number 7. Conclusion number 7 reads as follows: "The persons authorised to resolve all military and political issues in the Autonomous Region of Krajina are Vojo Kupresanin and Predrag Radic." Do you have any recollection of that conclusion, why it is that those two gentlemen are authorised to resolve all military and political issues in the ARK?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojo Kupresanin was probably named as the president of the assembly of the autonomous region. And Predrag Radic as the president of the Municipal Assembly of the largest municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why it is that Mr. Brdjanin didn't receive that authorisation?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's go to the very last entry. The very last entry is number 12. That appears to be the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let's go back to the previous one, Mr. Cunningham. This number 7, the assignment to Mr. Kupresanin and Mr. Radic of the authorisation, responsibility basically, to resolve all the, not just some, but all, the military and political issues in the ARK. Do you consider this as a heavy assignment? A heavy responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It probably was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it heavier than being president of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Vojo Kupresanin was healthy enough to take over such a responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, by virtue of this conclusion, he was appointed. He was assigned this responsibility. Whether he was really able to discharge it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let me go to the same exhibit, to the next entry, entry number 10, the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff, 14 May 1992. And sir, I want you to look at number 1, read it to yourself, because this again deals with disarmament.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Has the topic changed? By that I mean: Are we talking about all paramilitary groups or just non-Serb paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: What about number 5? Read number 5 to yourself because this has to deal with the financing of the republican institutions on ARK territory.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That refers to what I said a moment ago. Funds were not paid into the republican budget. Contributions and dues were instead paid to funds inside the region, to the SDK, the social accountancy service or the government auditing agency of the region. And from these funds, pensions were paid, healthcare, police, education, and other institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next entry, which is the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff meeting held 15 May 1992. I'm going to talk to you about entry number 3 which reads as follows: "Especially strict measures shall be implemented against any person misusing the uniform and insignia of the police, the TO, or the army and, without authorisation, stopping or checking people's identities or vehicles, searching dwellings or other premises." Was that conclusion directed at Serbs or non-Serbs, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paramilitary units were meant. Probably Serb paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next entry on Prosecutor's Exhibit 227. These are the conclusions of 18 May 1992. It says: "The Crisis Staffs are now the highest organs of authority in the municipalities." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Looking at number 4, this is another provision dealing with disarming paramilitaries. Number 6 is also something to deal with the disarming of the paramilitaries. I'm going to read number 4 out loud. "All formations that are not in the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the Banja Luka security service centre and are in the ARK are considered paramilitary formations and must be disarmed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "All those who are not part of the armed forces of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina or its police must return their weapons." Considering the language there, is that language directed towards Serb paramilitary or non-Serb paramilitaries? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to entry number 13, the last two conclusions of 20 May 1992 Crisis Staff meeting read as follows. Number 8 says: "All municipalities must contribute adequate funding for the security service centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." Number 9 reads: "All municipalities must immediately pay in funds for the financing of the institutions of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." You told us earlier that individuals didn't pay money into the ARK by 20 May 1992. Does this appear to be another request for money?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Well, you were there. What's your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that not all municipalities were paying these taxes and contributions that were due. And the funds available were insufficient to pay out pensions, to finance education, healthcare, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Were you aware of any sanctions that were ever imposed or penalties imposed on those municipalities that were not paying these taxes and contributions that were due?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no sanctions could be prescribed because the taxes and contributions were payable under republican legislation. The law on sales tax stipulates very precisely who is sanctionable in case of failure to pay. It was strictly legislated. It did not depend on anybody's will.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you know whether if the ARK Crisis Staff had the authority or the competence, the legal authority or the legal competence to sanction member municipalities for not paying?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could not do that. The ARK Crisis Staff had no legal tool to sanction anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you say "they had no legal tool," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody could be dismissed if they didn't apply this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And why couldn't they be dismissed? Did the ARK have the power to do that or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: ARK Crisis Staff. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very simply put, even if somebody failed to comply, there were no penalties to be imposed. When taxes were paid, it is well known who is supposed to control that and see whether a person abides by the law or not. The body that controls it is the tax administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to entry number 17, page 29 of the English version of P227. The conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff meeting, 26 May 1992. Conclusion number 1 reads as follows: "The work of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina has absolute support since it is now the highest organ of authority in the Autonomous Region of Krajina, as the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina cannot function due to objective and subjective circumstances. "Decisions of the Crisis Staff are binding for all crisis staffs in the municipalities. "These decisions of the Crisis Staff shall be submitted for verification to the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina as soon as it is able to convene." I've read that to you. I want to make sure that you have that in front of you because I'm going to ask you questions about it. You were present at the ARK Crisis Staff meetings during this period. Do we still have the controversy between the municipalities in favour of regionalisation and those in favour of centralisation?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That remained the case until the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is why on either the 14th or the 15th of September, amendments were adopted to the constitution by which regions stopped existing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's get back to the controversy. Those -- at around this time period, which is 26 May 1992, in ARK Crisis Staff meetings, are there municipalities who are questioning the legal competence of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no written complaints. This thing transpired only in debates and discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. So to answer my question, are there or are there not people who are questioning the legal competence of the ARK Crisis Staff at the very meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let's go back to conclusion number 1 where it reads that "the work of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina has absolute support..." I'm going to stop right there. Did it have the absolute support of all the municipalities, the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since it is worded in this way, you can guess that it didn't enjoy the support of all the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And why do you say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the dislike on the part of the people who were either in favour of regionalisation or in favour of centralisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. The next clause in -- next segment of conclusion number 1 reads: "... Since it" - the ARK Crisis Staff - "is now the highest organ of authority in the Autonomous Region of Krajina." Was it the highest organ of authority?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why they felt, they, the members of the ARK Crisis Staff, felt it was necessary to reach a conclusion with this wording? Let me phrase it this way: If they claim to be the highest organ in the ARK, why do they have to keep saying it? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably because of the dislike and the division among the municipalities who were either in favour of regionalisation or centralisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next entry, which is in Prosecutor's 227, entry 18, English page 30, the conclusions of the Crisis Staff meeting of the ARK 27 May 1992, a number of conclusions. I'm going to read to you number 1 because I want to ask you a question about that. Number 1 of the conclusions reads as follows: "A maximum degree of cooperation is to be established between the civilian and military authorities." Earlier, there was a conclusion dealing with General Talic and how he was requested to have mandatory attendance, and that talked about the cooperation between civilian and military authorities. 27 May, when this conclusion is entered, do you know why this provision is put into the conclusions of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, there was no cooperation, at least no good cooperation. And the military even mobilised some of the deputies. According to the law which was then in force, deputies were not supposed to be mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Now, earlier you told us that I think it was Colonel Vujinovic attended the meetings in the place of General Talic. Do you have any recollection of any direct orders being given by the Crisis Staff to either Colonel Vujinovic or any other military member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you remember any direct orders ever being given by the ARK Crisis Staff to any member of the security organs who might have been a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you remember the military making any request on the Crisis Staff either for food or supplies or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let's go to entry number 23 in Prosecutor's 227.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: May I have just a minute, Your Honour. I've got the wrong conclusion. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Let's go back one conclusion to number 22. These are the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff 28 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Conclusion number 1 reads as follows: "The control of all black marketeering outlets, the illegal exchange of foreign currencies and illegal trade must be tightened." Do you remember if Mr. Brdjanin had any position one way or the other against black marketeering and illegal trade? Did he speak out against it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody fought against this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And would that include Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm done with Exhibit 227. I'm going to talk to him about Exhibit 258, which is the next publication, I guess, of the ARK Crisis Staff Gazette. Actually, it's the ARK Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Entry 34 deals with the conclusions of the Crisis Staff reached at a meeting, 9 June 1992. Actually, it's a decision rather than a conclusion. Roman number I reads as follows: "In order to make more rational use of oil and oil products, the senior officials of the security service centre and the command corps shall impose immediate, absolute, and unconditional controls over the consumption of such products by significantly reducing the rather large number of transport units used and ceasing to using these vehicles immediately." Do you know what the response was from the police and the military with respect to this decision? Do you know whether it was ever followed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Are you aware of anyone ever reporting back from the police or the military as to whether or not they ever did anything to implement that decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to entry number 42 in P258. This is a decision from the ARK Crisis Staff at a meeting held 15 June 1992. Reads as follows: "Decision on amending and supplementing the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Article 1, paragraph 2 of the Article 35 of the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina - it gives the reference number - is hereby amended to read: `The decisions and conclusions of the Assembly must be respected by the municipalities.'" Article 2 gives the date that the law is to come into effect. Do you recall what the thought process was of the Crisis Staff as -- when they reached this decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statute of the autonomous region could be amended on the proposal of the assembly of the region, of the associated municipalities, and on the executive council. Here, the statute was not respected. This is contrary to the statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. What is the sense from the municipalities at this point? Are they respecting the ARK decisions? What can you tell us about that? You told us about the controversy between regionalisation and centralisation. I take it it's still going on at this juncture, correct, in 15 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cunningham can take what he likes, but what's the answer from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My question was I take it there was still the discussions over -- discussions between centralisation foes and regionalisation foes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: My objection to it is it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he has put the question once before, and it was allowed. And he is taking it week by week sort of. In some instances the witness said yes, he was aware of it, and other instances he said he was not aware of it. So maybe he can tell us now whether it was still on or not. Here he has, however, answered by saying that this division remained to the very end.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've sat here -- I don't want to give basic advocacy lessons, but the proper question is: Was there at this stage still discussion going on? Not, I take it there was. But Your Honour, I agree; I haven't objected so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically he has already answered the question, and I don't even see the need for the question being put again because he has already told you that this division, this discussion was there, remained until the very end, until practically September 12th or 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Well, I'll certainly honour Your Honour's directives. I have no problem doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: But my question is -- and it's in a different way. What is the attitudes towards the municipalities on 15 June 1992 with respect to the legal competence of the ARK Crisis Staff; that is, the legal ability of the ARK Crisis Staff to issue binding decisions? Are they respecting this, not respecting it? What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At their sessions, the municipalities had to adopt those. Whether they did that or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: But during this time period, when we're talking about -- I guess we're in mid-June, what is the sense of the municipalities? Are they respecting it or not respecting the ARK Crisis Staff decisions?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It transpires from this decision since the statute was amended, one may conclude that they didn't respect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Cunningham. How was this statute before and how is it amended now? Am I correct in stating that the statute required before being amended that decisions and conclusions taken by the Crisis Staff were to be validated, approved, by the municipal assemblies, by the respective municipal assemblies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were the municipal assemblies meeting at the time? Or were they in hibernation because of the existence of crisis staffs in all the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably they had to freeze their activities, so there were no sessions due to the government's decision on the establishment of crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So wouldn't it have been logical and reasonable in a time of great crisis that the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina to make sure that the decisions and conclusions are adopted, are implemented, that the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina be amended? Since the municipal assemblies were not meeting, and therefore could not adopt or approve the decisions taken by the ARK Crisis Staff, was that the situation to be accepted, to be kept, to be tolerated in a time of crisis, or a situation which needed a remedy, the remedy being the amendment to the statute that was adopted on decision number 42?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the assemblies could not hold their meetings, then the crisis staff of each municipality was supposed to ratify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I would take it that if I were to show you documents of conclusions of decisions taken by the municipal crisis staffs adopting, endorsing the decisions taken by the ARK Crisis Staff, would that mean that the municipalities were implementing the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff, or not to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they ratified them at their sessions, I suppose they were then in a position to implement them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Following up on Mr. President's questions to you, do you know what percentage -- do you have any idea of the percentage of ARK Crisis Staff decisions that were implemented? Do you have any way of knowing that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Were you aware in the time that you were on the Crisis Staff and working with it on a regular basis of the ARK Crisis Staff ever sanctioning a specific municipality or any municipality for failing to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. implement any of their decisions?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. I'm done with -- while we're talking about ARK Crisis Staff meetings, let me ask you: To the best of your recollection, do you ever remember any discussion about Manjaca or any of the other camps at ARK Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you remember the representatives from -- first of all, what was the attitude of the Prijedor Municipality towards the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They showed dislike towards the people and the work of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And how did that dislike manifest itself? Were you aware of any written decisions by, for example, the Prijedor Crisis Staff relating to the ARK -- the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any decisions that were passed in Prijedor. But this dislike was very obvious at the meetings. It transpired very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And how did it transpire? How did it manifest or show itself at the meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They emphasised the principle of centralisation whereas the others emphasised the principle of regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Other than the Prijedor Municipality, do you know what municipalities joined with them in the -- on the principle of centralisation?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some, but I can't remember which ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let me see if I can jog your memory. What about Sanski Most? Do you have any recollection of what their position was?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: How about Krupa?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: How about Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: During specific Crisis Staff meetings, were you and the members of the Crisis Staff given information, for example, about the clashes in Prijedor around Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember any.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: During your testimony today, you and I have -- you've discussed and referred to decisions that were published in Prosecutor's 227, Prosecutor's 258, which are the ARK Gazette. Were those ARK Gazettes published and disseminated during the existence of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not disseminated. They could be purchased.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Well, after a meeting of the ARK Crisis Staff, if decisions and conclusions were reached, how were they -- how was the word spread? How did the municipalities find out?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they found out through their representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to go into a new subject that's a rather lengthy one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a break of 25 minutes starting from now. Usher, please could you accompany the witness first. Okay. 25 minutes from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: As the secretary to the ARK Crisis Staff, were you responsible for the actual drafting of these conclusions and decisions that we just have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Were you the individual also responsible for typing them up in the form that we see in the various exhibits that have been admitted to this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: After the decision or conclusions were in their final form and ready for signature, what would happen? What was your -- what did you do?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we published them in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did the -- was it necessary for -- to obtain some signatures on the decisions or conclusions?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes yes; sometimes not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let's talk about the times that it was done. Would you take these decisions and conclusions and present them to the defendant for his signature or to someone else for his or her signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was usually I who did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. And of the decisions and conclusions that were presented, do you remember how many the defendant signed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay, let's go ahead and refresh your recollection by looking at the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I apologise. This is going to take a little bit, Your Honour. The exhibit to look at -- I'm working on a spreadsheet, Your Honour, because our database was down last night and I couldn't pull off the specific documents. The first exhibit would be P175, decision of 6 May 1992. And what I'm going to ask you to do, sir, is to look at the -- Mr. Usher, there's going to be a string of decisions that are going to be in this same range, between 175 up to 241 -- 243. The bulk of them will be in that range, just to assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You should have Exhibit P175 in front of you. Do you recognise that signature? Do you know whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The next exhibit I want to show you is Exhibit P179, 8 May 1992 conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff. I want to ask you if you recognise that signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is obviously a matter for Mr. Cunningham. But if he's going to do this exercise, it may be sensible, he gave us a list of all the documents that appear to do with Brdjanin's signature. I don't know if he wants to look at Exhibit 176 because that's the next one --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: No, I don't intend on doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. Thank you, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature as the defendant's?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to P183, 9 May 1992 conclusion. Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 18 -- Prosecutor's 182, and I'll ask you the same question. This is a decision, 9 May, ARK Crisis Staff, 1992. Again, do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Is it the defendant's signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: All right. And you do recognise Mr. Brdjanin's signature; you've seen it many, many times before, or have you? Let me rephrase it so it's not leading. Do you recognise Mr. Brdjanin's signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I just want to make sure. Okay. The next exhibit would be 185. Conclusions, 11 May 1992. Is that the defendant's signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. After this, let's look at P187. Decision, 11 May 1992. Is that the defendant's signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you say you're not sure, what do you mean by that? Do you recognise it as his signature? You mean, you tell us you know it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand this. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer because the interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the question, is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: This is going to be a series of questions. It's going to be the same thing. I'm trying to establish if these are the defendant's signatures on these documents that I'm putting in front of you. So the question is a very, very simple one: Is this his signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure because there were a lot of people at that time who may have faked his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did you ever sign for him?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Let's now look at P184. This is 11 May 1992, information related to travel permits. Do you recognise that to be the defendant's signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Does it appear to be his signature? Is it close, or what are you not so sure about?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whose signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at P192, please. Yes, 13 May 1992 conclusion. Do you recognise whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Mr. Brdjanin's?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My question is do you recognise that signature as belonging to a specific --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand whose signature you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why you're getting confused. What you have right in front of you, what does it show there? There's a stamp; there's a name; there's a signature. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see that, and I'm not sure whose signature it is. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to P191. I'll ask you the same question. Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. I'll ask you the same question with respect to P198, 14 May 1992 instructions dealing with a duty rota. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this is Mr. Brdjanin's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Next exhibit will be P194, 14 May 1992 conclusion. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. The next exhibit will be P200, 15 May 1992 statement regarding curfews. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Next exhibit will be P199, this is 15 May 1992, a conclusion dealing with curfew. And again, sir, whose signature is that? Actually, that doesn't appear to have a signature. Well, the good news is -- well, I won't say anything. The next exhibit will be P210. This is 27 May 1992, conclusion. Do you recognise -- I'm glad to see there's a signature and ask you if you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a minute, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And ask the witness a very simple question. Was there anyone else authorised to sign these conclusions, apart from the president, apart from Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, any member of the Crisis Staff could have signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. Could you sign any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that I was authorised to sign.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On what do you base your conclusion that any member of the Crisis Staff was authorised to sign these conclusions? On what do you base --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, sometimes after a session was over, if Mr. Brdjanin had to leave very quickly because he had prior other engagements, then somebody else could have signed for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next exhibit would be P532, 3 June 1992, decision. This regards Atlas Travel. Just for the usher's benefit, the next exhibits will be in the range of 230 to -- roughly up to 273.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Is that Mr. Brdjanin's signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Next exhibit will be P232, 8 June 1992 decision. Do you see a signature there? Okay. Move to the next exhibit, which is going to be P238, conclusions, 9 June 1992. I'll ask you the same question when you get it: Is that Mr. Brdjanin's signature if indeed there is a signature on that form?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Next exhibit would be P295, 9 June 1992 decision dealing with employment matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham, Ms. Korner, I need to suspend the sitting for a couple of minutes. In the meantime, perhaps if you give the list to the usher --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- We can prepare. This list, we can hand the documents straight away to the witness, and he can then simply identify from amongst those documents any in which Mr. Brdjanin's signature he recognises.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's a wonderful suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- and you can stay here. --- Break taken at 11.22 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think if we finish the exercise --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think we're coming close, Your Honour. I've given him a list, put it in chronological order. And he's also, because I couldn't access these documents last night, checking to see if there's a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And our usher, I can assure you is an extremely efficient person. I told him so yesterday, that his help -- yes, I see. Mr. Nicholls, one moment. His efficiency contributes to the better running of the proceedings and I appreciate that. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just a completely different subject, Your Honours had suggested that Mr. Brown look for documents on two topics based on his cross-examination. Yesterday we were to give you a deadline, and in everything that happened, we didn't. And we forget to tell you. I apologise. Last night, I called Mr. Brown and just asked him how long he would need, and he would ask until next Friday. Not tomorrow, a week from tomorrow, and he'll submit whatever documentation he can find on those two matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, so it would be Friday the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then for the record, Mr. Brown has until Friday, the 7th of November to furnish the Trial Chamber with additional information reference to which was made in one of the last two sittings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, following your suggestion, what we're doing is we're pulling all the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's what we need. Because going through each document one by one sometimes only to discover that there is not even a signature, I think it's a cumbersome procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It's tantalising testimony, I'm sure everybody's just enthralled by it, but I appreciate the Court's suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Once he has singled them out if any at all, he will hand them to us, we will have them verified by the Prosecution, by yourself, and by us, and we will put them on record. Now, witness, Mr. Blagojevic, what I want you to do is this: You are going to look through a series of documents on which supposedly there is a signature. I want you to go through each one of these documents. And if you recognise Mr. Brdjanin's signature on any of them, please keep that document separate. And at the end of this exercise, you will hand to the usher all those documents on which you have recognised Mr. Brdjanin's signature. The others, you put aside for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you are ready tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you please give to the usher all the documents on which you have recognised Mr. Brdjanin's signature. How many? Just one document. Can I have a look at it, usher, please, before I show it to the Prosecution, to the Defence, and then we'll put it on the ELMO. Yes, usher, could you show it to Ms. Korner, please. That's the same document. I mean, it's two copies of the same document. Could you show the document, please, to Mr. Cunningham. Yes, and usher, could I ask you, please, to put the document, both pages, one after the other on the ELMO so that the accused himself has a look at it, and the public. Yes, could we see the other one, please. All right. Could you hand them back to me, please. For the record, the witness has identified Document Exhibit Number P255b.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just confirm, that the number of the decision is 03-531/92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It has been exhibited twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly this is why. Which refers precisely to decision 3-531/92 dated 22nd of June of 1992. Yes, usher, you can have this document back. And could I have the other -- all the other documents, please. And for the record, the other documents which were shown to the witness and on which he did not recognise the signature of Mr. Brdjanin are document having ERN number in B/C/S, 01061766, referring to the decision numbered 03-486/92, dated 17th of June 1992. Exhibit Number P243, which refers to decision number 03-562/92 dated 12th June 1992; Exhibit Number P273, referring to decision number 03-604/92, dated 2nd July 1992; document bearing ERN number 0057384 -- 3850 which -- on which there is no indication as to the date of the decision; document Exhibit Number P260 referring to decision number 03-361/92 dated 24th of June 1992; document Exhibit Number P254 which refers to "Leaders only loyal Serbs," an article in a newspaper, dated 22nd June 1992 having as a title: "Leaders only loyal Serbs"; document with ERN number 00880271 referring to decision number 03-457/92 dated 12th June 1992; Exhibit Number P239 referring to decision 03-465/92 dated 11th June 1992; and finally, document in B/C/S having ERN number 00880273 referring to decision 03-579/92 dated 12th June 1992. You can have them all back, usher. And again, once more, I thank you. And I thank you also, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Don't get in a hurry, Judge, because I have one more document I forgot to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No major calamity.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I don't think he was shown P46, which is a 24 June 1992 decision, and I also want to ensure he was shown P1725. And the usher has told me he was shown that document. So P46, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is Mr. Brdjanin's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm done with that exhibit, Your Honour. And I have just two final, brief areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sir, obviously when we looked at those documents, we saw that there were seals on them, on or near the signature. Who kept the seal for the ARK Crisis Staff? Was that your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statute, it was. However, we had an assistant. She was the one who was in charge of keeping the seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Was it a seal for the ARK Crisis Staff or a seal for the ARK Assembly, or do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was seal of the Assembly of the autonomous region. The Crisis Staff never had its seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, the final area, if I could go into private session to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are back in open session. And Mr. Cunningham hasn't got any further questions for you, which brings us to the cross-examination. And you are now going to be cross-examined by Ms. Korner, who is lead counsel in this case for the Prosecution. Your duty as a witness, even if you are a witness of the Defence, produced by the accused, your duty is to answer all the questions that Ms. Korner will put to you as fully and as truthfully as you can, as possible, in accordance with the oath that you took at the beginning of your testimony. In other words, my duty is to make it clear to you that the fact that you came here because the Defence brought you over to give testimony does not entitle you to draw a distinction between Mr. Brdjanin and his interests and the interests of the Prosecution. Your duty is to answer all questions irrespective of where they are coming from, truthfully in accordance with your oath. That's unless I dispense you from answering any questions. In fact, if there are any questions that you think you ought not to answer because of one reason or another, then you refer to me, and I will consult with my two Judges, and we will take a decision on whether you should answer that question or not. Ms. Korner, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, the events of the spring to autumn 1992 must have been some of the most dramatic that you have lived through. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had even more dramatic moments later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But 1992, April through to September, was the first time for you, was it not, that you had been involved in a situation where conflict was taking place in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you were in a position to see how the authorities were attempting to deal with that conflict?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you came to this Court to give evidence, was it your intention to try and assist the Court as much as you can with describing what happened?
