utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you find yourself, is this correct, in a position where you are wholly unable to remember the detail of those dramatic events?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a long time ago, Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When were you first asked to testify on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, was it a month ago, two months ago, two years ago?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it would be sooner two years than anything else, but I can't say that for a fact. I can't remember exactly when it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you were asked to testify for Mr. Brdjanin, were you asked if you had any documents available?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you have any documents from which you could refresh your memory about those events?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in July of 2001. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before coming to this court, were you able to either read any kind of record of that interview or listen to any tape recording of that interview?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was it? Written or oral? In other words, did you hear a tape or did you read it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just read, and I believe that it was only a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you read the part that was supplied you by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: To inform the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: He had access to his Rule 68 statement from us. That's all we had from the Prosecutor, and I want to make that clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. And my inquiry is slightly different directed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anybody in the authorities enable you to listen to your interview? And by "the authorities," I mean the authorities in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, July of 2001 was not the first time, was it, that you had met representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You first met representatives, didn't you, in April of 1996?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If I put the names of the people that you met to you, do you think you would remember them?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did they meet with you in the municipal building in Mr. Radic's conference room?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you there, if you can remember, for something like two hours?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you asked questions then about the Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly and the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that we spoke about that as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you tell the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor that the legal basis for the existence of the Autonomous Region of Krajina was the Amendment 42 to Article 276 of the Bosnia-Herzegovina constitution?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that was your understanding as a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you also tell them that the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region began working when war broke out in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked, weren't you, to provide documents in connection with both the Assembly of the Autonomous Region, and then the ARK -- then the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you provided a number of documents which related to the assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name Grant MacIntosh?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you have with you at this meeting a folder?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which contained documents which you declined to give copies of to the representatives?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because they asked you, didn't they, if they could see the documents that were in that folder, and you said that they didn't need to see that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I remember. They asked for my private folder. It was a folder given to me by a client of mine who asked me to try and exchange his property.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why had you brought that folder to a meeting with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor who were investigating the matters that had occurred within the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having had that folder with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I asked you whether you'd had a folder with you which you declined to show the representatives what was in it, and you said you remembered it was something to do with your private client.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, what I'm saying is that I don't know whether I had that particular folder with me as I came to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's start again. Did you have a folder with you which contained documents which you refused to let the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor see?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I had this folder on me at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Stop, Ms. Korner, because I'm getting annoyed with this. Earlier on, Ms. Korner asked you a very simple question, after that you had stated that you couldn't remember having a folder, couldn't remember having declined to give copies or to make available what you had in that folder, after all that you said -- Ms. Korner told you: "Because they asked you, didn't they, if they could see the documents in that folder because you said that they didn't need to see that?" And you said: "Now, I remember. They asked for my private folder. It was a folder given to me by a client of mine who asked me to try and exchange his property." Did you have it with you or not? Because you didn't say you remember now that you had a folder, but that you also was asked -- you were asked to show what you had in that folder and that you declined to show it. So you can't remember and forget at the same time. I mean, you'll be the first one that I have come across that is capable of doing that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the following day, when they arrived on the following day, they asked for a folder from a filing cabinet. In the meantime, the client had come and taken the folder away. I don't know whether I had that folder on me when I came to the meeting with them. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when you said "now I remember." I'll read it out again to you. When you were asked -- I repeat it again. Ms. Korner told you: "Because they asked you, didn't they, if they could see the documents in that folder and you said that they didn't need to see that?" And your answer was, referring to a specific day and a specific incident when you were in the office of Mr. Radic. And you answered: "Now I remember. They asked for my private folder. It was a folder given to me by a client of mine who asked me to try and exchange his property." They wouldn't have asked you for that folder if you didn't have it with you, would they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When I returned from that office, there was a folder on a shelf, and then they inquired about that folder. And then I told them, "I'm sorry, the folder contains some private documents."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You knew, didn't you, Mr. Blagojevic, that what the investigators wanted was documents which related to the operation of the assembly, and then the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And on that day, everything that was there was handed over.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you this, Mr. Blagojevic: Was what was in that folder which you refused to let the representatives see, did that contain the minutes of the meetings of the Crisis Staff of the region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's because according to you, no minutes were ever taken. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'll come back to that a little later. Now, I want to start with these -- your actual employment so that we can try and make sense out of what you said yesterday. But before I do that, can I just ask you this: During this period, were you reading the newspaper Srpski Glas?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why? Why rarely? It was the only newspaper really available, wasn't it, in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. But I read them very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was preparing for my bar exam, so I had no time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period, please, from March 1992 until September.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's when you were preparing for your bar exams?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, yes, yes, it was the bar exam.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought you'd already qualified as a lawyer some years ago, or some years before that.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I had qualified before involved a specialist exam which is a part of the bar exams.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to press on that. In addition to that, did you also, when there was electricity, watch television?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And listen to the radio?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did when I had the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we look, please, at how you came to be employed by the assembly. What you said yesterday was, I'm afraid, slightly confused as far as we're concerned. So can I ask you now to have a look, please, at a document which is P6.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are some documents I'm afraid that I'm going to ask the witness to look at which are not on my list, but that one was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, that's an excerpt from the minutes of the 6th Session of the Bosnian Krajina Community of Municipalities on the 6th of September. And if we go to item number 3 -- I'm sorry, usher, you have to pull it up on the agenda, right at the bottom of the page. I'm sorry, usher, you have to put it up so that we see the bottom of the page. On mine, it's all on one page. Can you turn it over. Number 3, okay. Thank you. "After the Bosnian Krajina Community of Municipalities Assembly president made the introductory remarks, Boro Blagojevic, a lawyer who has worked for several years in the municipal assembly as the director of the department for inspection and determining of public revenues was unanimously elected secretary of the Bosnian Krajina Community of Municipalities Assembly." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You started work on the 6th of September. It states there you had worked for several years in the municipal assembly as the director of the department for inspection and determining of public revenues. Was that the Municipal Assembly of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was the Bosanski Brod Municipality. And I wasn't the director. I worked first as an inspector, and then became head of that tax department.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. It may not matter. Now, you told Mr. Cunningham yesterday that you worked for some months, or that's the way it seemed, as the secretary to the community of municipalities. Well, now, can you have a look, please, at P12.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, if Ms. Korner has an updated list of exhibits, I'd like to get it during the break because 12 wasn't on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have an updated list, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't. I'm afraid I just picked up some scrawled -- they are all going to go on the ELMO. And in fact, some of them were on Mr. Cunningham's list but weren't used by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If this at any time causes you a problem, Mr. Cunningham, let us know. But I don't believe it should.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the break, I can write up the extra ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that's the minutes of the assembly of the community of municipalities on the 16th of September? And item number 1 on the agenda, the adoption of a decision to declare the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So all in all, you worked for the association of the community -- I'm sorry. The association of Bosnian Krajina municipalities for a total period of ten days?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And after that, you were the secretary to the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because it was only a question of renaming the autonomous region. It used to be the association of municipalities, and it was renamed autonomous region, but the responsibilities and duties remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but as a lawyer, there was a difference, wasn't there? Because the autonomous regions, as such, did not exist under the BiH constitution.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The constitution speaks of the association of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And I want to come on to the legalities of all of this in a moment. But in any event, am I right also in thinking that your acquiring of this job as secretary to whatever it was called, assembly or community, was obtained for you by Predrag Radic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That's not through Predrag Radic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with Mr. Radic about this before you took the job as secretary?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had talked to his chef du cabinet. In fact, I made inquiries before that about vacancies in the Municipal Assembly. I was interested.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So it's wrong, is it, to say that you found out about the job of secretary at the end of August 1991 when you ran into Mr. Radic at the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I found out about it earlier, in August. That's when I found out about the vacancy in the Self-managed Regional Community of Banja Luka. That's how it was registered it the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. This is a simple question. Did you have any discussions with Mr. Radic about this position?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. None at all. I didn't even know Mr. Radic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we look now at what your job description was. Could you have a look, please, at the statute of the assembly rather than of the Community of Bosnian Krajina Municipalities, which is P80, although I accept that it's identically worded. And can you have a look, please, and can we have up Article Number 30, which is on page 10 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Does that set out the duties of the secretary, to assist the president in his work; supervise the preparation of sessions or prepared - I'm not sure that's a good translation, but anyhow - the executive council..." Now, did your job, therefore, include helping to draft the agenda? Helping the president to draft the agenda?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Making sure that items which were suggested by other members of the assembly were communicated to the president, items for the agenda, I should say?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Making sure that the sessions were properly minuted and recorded?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: For that, did you employ a technical secretary or was there a technical secretary employed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that at the beginning, there wasn't one. And later on, I can't remember when it was. I believe it was in March that we may have employed somebody. But I can't remember. In any case, up to then, there was nobody. But there was a secretary to Mr. Kupresanin. However, she was not an employee of Krajina. She was an employee of the municipal assembly who would sometimes help me with some things because I was on my own obviously.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But the importance of minutes of these meetings was so that it could be seen how decisions had been arrived at. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We would draw up minutes, and then this thing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who had spoken either in favour or against a motion, a decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this was standard, was it not, for any body of authority in the former Yugoslavia, municipal assembly, committees, whatever?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, as secretary, your job was an important one, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was important or not because at that time, there was no proper financing of the municipality, of the municipal assembly. It did not really operate as a body of authority. Can you imagine the assembly of the autonomous region which has only one employee? It's not even serious. It was simply unable to function as an important institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whether or not it actually was able to function is neither here nor there. Within the terms of that assembly and its statute, your job as secretary was an important one. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was the only one who had this responsibility. I was the one who was in charge of preparing all that, and I could not transfer my duties to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, while we're dealing with the statute, can you have a look, please, at Article Number 16. That article was also in the statute of the Bosnian communities, but says: "The Autonomous Region of Krajina shall monitor the situation and coordinate activities for the organisation and implementation of preparations for All Peoples' Defence in accordance with the law, municipal defence plans, and the republican defence plan." That article was something that did not appear, did it, in any of the earlier associations of communities?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether that language also featured in the statute of the association of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, it did. But I'm talking about the earlier ones. Before the Krajina association of municipalities, the earlier associations of municipalities allowed for under the law did not have any provisions as to defence, did they? They were economic only.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you took the job, did you read the statute of the association?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you notice this particular provision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you query why an association that was only economic should have something in its statute about defence?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, because it did sound odd.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who did you ask about it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask anyone. It's just that it seemed a little odd to me as I was reading article by article. I wondered to myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you didn't think that you should ask, perhaps, Mr. Kupresanin, or Mr. Brdjanin, the vice-president of the association, why an economic association had something in it about defence?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In December of -- I'm sorry, in November -- no, I better go back. In December of 1991, did the constitutional court of Bosnia rule upon that particular provision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a motion was made to review the constitutionality of this decision. But I'm not sure of the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At the time, would you have been informed as the secretary and as a lawyer of what the decision was?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you can't remember anything about the decision of the constitutional court?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I did not receive Official Gazettes of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I really didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But as far as you were concerned, after -- certainly after November 1991, the assembly of the autonomous region was a legally constituted body, having been approved by the second assembly of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 21st of November. I think that was the date, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Mr. Blagojevic. It was the 21st of November. So as far as you were concerned, the assembly was legal and your job was legal.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the fact that assemblymen had approved the statute and they were elected assemblymen, deputies from assemblies adopted the statute which was verified, I worked there, I had no other job.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. No, no. I mean, there's no trick about this, Mr. Blagojevic. Regardless of whether or not the declaration of the Serbian republic was legal, but as far as you were concerned, the Serbian assembly, 21st of November, had verified all the autonomous regions?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us that the assembly contained not just Serb delegates. That's what you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can you have a look, please, at a list that you, in fact, provided to the Office of the Prosecutor, which is Exhibit P61. That is on my list, yes. Do you remember giving the representatives this list?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want you to just have a quick look through it. Actually I'll tell you what --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If Your Honours will take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The question I want you to answer after the break is this,

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: If you can point to any delegate who is not of Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think there shouldn't be any problem with having the witness remain in possession of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've got lots of copies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: During the break, have a coffee. Go through it. Just don't mark -- or at least we can have a photocopy of it, and to help you, you can mark on the photocopy, and then you can come back to us and indicate who was not of Serb ethnicity. All right? The usher will make a photocopy of the document. You go through it during the break and do exactly what I have told you to do. Yes, usher, you may escort the witness, prepare the photocopy for him. And we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you've had a chance now to look at this document. Can you tell me - if I can find my own copy - anyone who's not a Serb or from a declared Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here under Prnjavor municipality, there is Mehmed Sabic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Usher, could you just put on the ELMO the document from the very -- just start from page 1, but at the top, because -- let's -- okay. What I require from you as you start mentioning names, since the list also shows a number plus the name plus the municipality, you will follow the same order. For example, if you're going to refer to number 12, Mehmed Sabic, you would say representative number 12, Mehmed Sabic from the municipality of Prnjavor. And then you go on from there one by one as you identify them. All right? Go ahead. And I don't think Ms. Korner needs to interrupt you each time. So you can go down the list. Starting from the top, each time there is one from non-Serb ethnicity, you just indicate him to us, or her.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 12, Prnjavor Municipality; number 27, Bosanska Gradiska; number 31 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, mention the name. 27, Stjepan Kozjan from Bosanska Gradiska. Would this be a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this person is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 31, Bosanska Gradiska, Edin Biscevic, a Bosniak. Number 32, Dzevdet Kozarcanin in Bosanska Gradiska, a Bosniak. Number 52, Nezir Karahodzic, a Bosniak. Number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Glamoc. Number 58 from Bosanska Dubica, Bakir Karabegovic. And I have not identified anybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, back to you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, with the exception of the six people you've identified, everybody else was a Serb?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you give us a date of this list? There's no date on it. A rough idea of when this list would have been compiled.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is a list that belonged to the association of municipalities. Those were the delegates that represented the association of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it actually says: "List of representatives in the Krajina Autonomous Region Assembly."

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you mean that the representatives never changed over the period?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And Prijedor, if you look at page -- the third page, numbers 116 through to 122, can you tell us, please, who, if you can read it, who is the representative at number 120? And 121?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 120 is Pilipovic. And 121 is Kurnoga.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 119, that's Milomir Stakic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Prijedor had a number of Muslims, did it not?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was a Muslim majority municipality, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know whether that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But only Serbs, all these people who attended were Serbs, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that at that time, Prijedor was not a member of the assembly of the region. I really don't know how that it happened that these people were even able to attend the sessions, and I can also see here -- I don't know whether this means under 117, 118, 119, I don't know what this means. There's some sort of signs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Wasn't this, in fact, an organisation for gathering together the Serbs in the municipalities of the ARK?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statute, the assembly was supposed to be composed of the elected representatives of all the municipalities. I don't know whether these people here are elected representatives who were elected at the sessions of their respective municipal assemblies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Forget about what the statute says. In reality, and you were there on a daily basis, Mr. Blagojevic, wasn't this an organisation intended to pull together the Serbs within the municipalities of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was the objective.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you worked on a daily basis, didn't you, with Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Didn't it become apparent to you from the meetings and from your dealings with Mr. Kupresanin that that was what this organisation was for?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given my job, which was to prepare the meetings and the room where it was to be held, and then compile the minutes, I really wouldn't be able to tell you what the intention was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you had your meetings with Mr. Kupresanin, as the president of this assembly and of this region, didn't it become apparent to you that this organisation was nothing more than an excuse to pull together the Serbs in the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object, Your Honour. He has been asked that question twice, and twice he said he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained. Or if you want, Ms. Korner, rephrase the question in some other way. But basically, this is a repetition, an exact repetition of what you had asked him before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that may be right. I thought I was being rather lenient as far as Mr. Cunningham was concerned, but I'll move on because I don't want to waste any more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to go back to what you told us about how you came to get this job. And you told us -- you denied emphatically that it had nothing to do whatsoever with Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sanction is not working, Your Honour, so we'll put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you have a copy of the translation of your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor. Could you have, first of all, page 4 of the English on the ELMO. And B/C/S, we'll give you page -- I suppose we should have marked it. Yes, sorry, I can't for the moment see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would Your Honour forgive me. We were going to put it up over the ELMO, but we discovered over the break it's not working properly. Yes, okay, thank you, yes. It's page 5 in the B/C/S. Can we have page 4 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the bottom of our page 4, and if you can find the part where the investigator, Mr. Inayat, asked you: "Okay, are you aware that at that point when you moved to Banja Luka, there was already an institution here in Banja Luka called the Community of the Bosanska Krajina Municipalities?" Your reply: "No, I didn't know about it." Mr. Inayat asked you,"When did you learn about it?" "I found out about it at the end of August, when I bumped into the president of the municipality, Mr. Radic, when I went to the Municipal Assembly in Banja Luka." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's on the next --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, it's on the next page. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What we need to see for the time being is the top of page 5. Thank you, Judge Taya.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. What I want to understand -- well, first of all, do you agree that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It says here that I met Mr. Zoran Joldzic, not the president of the Municipal Assembly, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the first time that we've had this problem this way because of course the interview was recorded in English, and this is a translation that we had done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I have the page back for a moment. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you have a look, please, page 5, line 7. Sorry, line 12.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says here: "I learned that at the end of August when I bumped into the then chief of the cabinet of the president of municipality, Mr. Radic."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In your translation, and it may well be we have to get back the original tape for this, but does it say "I found out about it" - i.e. the Bosnian Krajina Municipalities - "at the end of August when I bumped into president of the municipality, Mr. Radic"?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not President Radic, but the chief of his cabinet, and this is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I have a look at the B/C/S version, please. Yes, basically, I have a confirmation from Judge Janu who can understand the language that what indeed is stated here is that the witness met with the chef du cabinet of President Radic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour. I do apologise. I apologise to Mr. Blagojevic. I'm making a bad point. We'll check the tape, but I had hoped that we had already done a check between the two versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's no major --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, it wasn't Mr. Radic you met, but the chef du cabinet. And who was the chef du cabinet?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. Zoran Joldzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he was the person who suggested you should apply for the job. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that there was a vacancy in the self-management interest community. I asked him whether there was a vacancy in the municipal assembly, and he told me that there was one but that that one was in the self-management interest community.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's move on because clearly the point I want to make is not a good one. All right. Now, we've dealt with the membership of the assembly. The assembly itself did have actual power, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statute, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. No, no. In reality, it had actual power, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not organised at the time. It had just one professional member of staff, and it was really hard to see it as an organisation that could function properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Forget about for the moment whether it actually was well organised or disorganised; it had actual, real power, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In keeping with the statute, it did. Again, in keeping with the statute.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, the statute gave it power. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The autonomous regions were verified on November the 21st?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it exercised the power that the statute gave it, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In keeping with the statute.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, can you have a look, please, now at Document P -- sorry, I'm just going to get this right. P159. Again, I think it's on my list. 'Tis, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Actually, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: According to the list Ms. Gustin is waving, it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I stand corrected. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision dated the 27th of April 1992. And can you have a look, please, there at the stamp, and perhaps you can tell us whether you recognise Mr. Kupresanin's signature.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You have no difficulty in recognising his signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was closer to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The -- while we're on the subject of signatures, although I will come back to it, if it's not signed by the person whose signature block appears on it, it has the word "za," doesn't it, by it, which I think means "on behalf of"?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the customary procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when a decision was sent to the Official Gazette, did it have by the signature the letters "SR"?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'll come back to that. All right. Mr. Kupresanin, on the 27th of April 1992, is making a decision, or the assembly is, signed by the president I should say that there should be a special police detachment formed within the Banja Luka security services. And the explanation for it is given at the back of that decision. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And indeed, a special police -- a special-purpose police detachment was formed, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you not remember --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you not remember an enormous parade in Banja Luka in May of this particular detachment?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So can we take it that it was formed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to look a little bit more at the powers of this assembly. Could you now have a look, please, at P118. Now, this should be an assembly you do remember, Mr. Blagojevic. If you look, please, at the end of the conclusions, does your signature as secretary appear there?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There's no signature. It just says "secretary" here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry. I haven't got the B/C/S in front of me. But your name appears there, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the secretary of the regional assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, this appears to be a copy because there are no signatures on either, either of you or Mr. Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me one moment. I just want to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this a document which is contested by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just checking, Your Honour, that it was one that was given to us by Mr. Blagojevic himself, but I can't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 118, isn't it? Now I'm trying to look at the provenance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's, Your Honour, I'm told -- yes, it was contested, so perhaps we can go through it then in a little bit more detail. It was used by Dr. Donia, interestingly enough, on the -- I see, it's the same as P35. Just a moment. Thank you. It's one of those, I'm afraid, where we gave two numbers, and we don't have the provenance of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I want to go through this then in a little detail. Do you remember this meeting? It was the meeting attended by Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Koljevic, and Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was probably at the meeting of the assembly of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I agree. That's what it says at the top. I'm asking you if you now remember a meeting of the assembly attended by the most senior Bosnian Serbs in the government, or some of the most senior?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I can see in the minutes is correct. They were indeed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Forget about the minutes for a moment. I'm asking you now if you recall, actually can visualise, that meeting attended by all -- I'm sorry, by some of the most senior Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a session of the assembly of the autonomous region. They were present, and they addressed the representatives who were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you remember that the reason they were there is because there was talk of the Krajina becoming an independent republic joining together with the Croatian Krajina, the RSK?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can't see this -- what I can't see here is when it was held, the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 29th of February of 1992, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a session of the regional assembly where the deputies or the MPs wanted to separate themselves and form an independent state of Krajina. That's what happened at that session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was where the clash happened between the region and the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this is one of the documents, in fact, isn't it, Mr. Blagojevic, that you gave to Mr. Grant MacIntosh?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what I want to look at, please, in this, there was a discussion in which Mr. Kupresanin and Mr. Brdjanin spoke. And then the conclusion, can you look at that, please. It's on the second page. Mr. Cizmovic, the coordinator in the Serbian government of BH recalled the that the Autonomous Region of Krajina can draw its autonomy from the recently adopted constitution of the Serbian Republic and that if a republic of Krajina were declared, all Serbs outside this territory would suffer from the consequences of this decision. In other words, Mr. Blagojevic, what Mr. Cizmovic was emphasising was the Autonomous Region of Krajina had sufficient power under the constitution and did not need -- and under the Serb constitution and therefore didn't need to become an independent republic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And just so -- if we look at the next conclusion, we see there's conclusions. And then over the next page for us in English: "The deputies in the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina accepted the constitution. "Two, the status of the Autonomous Region of Krajina will be incorporated into the constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH in accordance with its practical needs in order to achieve its free economic development. "Three, establish immediately strict control of the territory [Realtime transcript read in error "Territorial Defence"] of the autonomous region." What was meant by that, Mr. Blagojevic? I'm sorry. I see it's come out. It should read -- I didn't say Territorial Defence. "Establish strict control of the territory of the autonomous region." I think that has been properly translated. What was meant by that conclusion, Mr. Blagojevic? "Establish immediately strict control..." Strict control of what?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I want you to think hard. You were present at this meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was a meeting of major importance, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in light of the number of those present, it certainly was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was discussed that resulted in number 3 of the conclusions being established immediately "strict control of the territory"?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I don't know what that meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want you to think about it one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object. He's thought about it and answered twice. He says he can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it deserves a further -- a little bit of thinking, Mr. Cunningham. Think about the third time and try and answer the question, please. Can you follow the first two decisions? Can you recall those first two decisions and follow the logic in them based on the discussions that took place? Let's take them one by one. Do you recall the deputies present there accepting the constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH in full, without any reservation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you recall the deputies, all of them, because this was a unanimous decision with not even abstentions, 148 attended, out of 161 if I remember well, do you remember them deciding that, "The status of the ARK will be incorporated into" - status or the statute? I suppose it's the statute - "will be incorporated into the constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH in accordance with with its practical needs in order to achieve its free economic development." Do you recall this decision being taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says here that they accepted the constitution in full. Accepted. That means they had no jurisdiction to adopt the constitution on the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not answering --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rather, the republic of the Serbian people. Only MPs could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember the deputies present at that meeting agreeing, voting in favour of the decision that the status or statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina will be incorporated into the constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH in accordance with its practical needs in order to achieve its free economic development? Do you remember this decision being taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since they endorsed the constitution, and the constitution emphasised the existence of regions, then they probably did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do these first two decisions follow from the records of the debate that you see on the previous page, or pages? If you look at the minutes and see what Vojo Kupresanin said, what Brdjanin said, what Cizmovic said, what Karadzic said, are the first two decisions a natural and logical consequence of that debate? And of the statements made? Sorry to have taken him over from you for a while, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's quite all right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's look at the decision. It didn't fall from heaven. Must have been debated, too. Read that decision, please. Decision number 3. Do you tie it up, do you connect it with the first two decisions, with the previous two decisions? Do you remember that decision being taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was adopted on the 29th of February 1992. And it probably fitted into the entire discussion that took place at that session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I invite you to look back at the previous two pages where you see the record minutes of the statements made by Kupresanin, Brdjanin, Brdjanin again, Karadzic, Cizmovic, and Karadzic again. Take your time. Read the decision again. And can you now try to explain what it means on the basis of that debate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there a discussion in the assembly about the Serbs seizing power in municipalities where they did not hold overall power?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't recall. But that session was held precisely due to this clash between the region and the centre. And whether they debated this issue or not, I can't remember. Because it was really a major conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But the strict control of the territory of the ARK was to be established by whom?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know what was meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you have an expression in the Serbian language, "see no evil, hear no evil?"

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the meaning, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is that what you're trying to persuade us, Mr. Blagojevic, of today?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Excuse me, Judge. I'm going to object to the form of the question. Although put nicely, it is argumentative with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, rephrase your question, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you're not going to finish today. But I want you to think about this tomorrow -- until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who drafted this third decision and the minutes?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, who drafted it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drew up the minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So do I take it you drew up -- you formulate a sentence which doesn't make sense to you, which you say you don't even know what it is all about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I prepared a draft minutes based on the discussion. And then at the next session, my draft is presented to the delegates, and then it is up to them to accept my proposal, my draft, or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but when you wrote "establish control immediately -- strict control of the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina," what were you writing? What were you stating? What were you reporting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember what the discussion was about. I can't remember what was discussed, what gave rise to this item 3. I don't remember the gist of the discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm going to read part of the minutes, unless you want to read it yourself, Ms. Korner. I start with Jovan Cizmovic, Mr. Blagojevic. The interpreters would bear with me a couple of minutes, and we'll wind up after this question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Jovan Cizmovic, coordinator of the Serbian government of BH recalled that the Autonomous Region of Krajina can draw its autonomy from the recently adopted constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that if a republic of Krajina were declared, all Serbs outside this territory would suffer from the consequences of this decision. Radovan Karadzic stressed that it would be a crime against the Krajina if it were declared a republic. Those who advocate such childish ideas are exposing the Serbian people to trouble. The Bosnian Krajina does not need any national councils, since it has legally elected organs, and the republican Serbian authorities are fully functioning." Does it give you a lead as to what was decided in the part where you report that a decision was taken to establish immediately strict control over the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll stop there and continue tomorrow, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I just perhaps ask Mr. Blagojevic before tomorrow over the afternoon to think about what happened during those meetings of the Crisis Staff, because he is going to be asked further questions tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I need an updated exhibit list from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you will hand it --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Mr. Blagojevic. You'll return to this courtroom tomorrow morning at 9.00. In the meantime, Mr. Usher will escort you. Thank you. I should like again once more to thank the interpreters, the technicians and all the staff for staying with us a few minutes beyond the scheduled time limit. I thank you. And we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning.
